commits.edited_message:
[raster] Clip the edge sweep's column walk to the surface (#6251)

* [raster] Clip the edge sweep's column walk to the surface

edge_sweep_row() walked every fixed-point pixel column an edge spans,
even though columns right of the surface contribute nothing and
columns left of it only contribute a cover delta that telescopes into
column 0.  A near-horizontal edge with extreme coordinates could span
~2^24 columns per row, making sweep cost proportional to coordinate
range instead of surface width: the ClusterFuzz testcase took 114s in
a plain release build.

Fold the left-of-surface portion of the walk into a single column-0
cover update, skip the right-of-surface portion, and enter/exit the
per-column loop at the visible window.  Jumping the incremental fy
accumulator by k*delta_fy is exact, since the increment is constant
and the running sums are bounded, so output is bit-identical; verified
by comparing 178 hb-raster renders (draw and paint paths, several
fonts, sizes, and negative-margin crops that clip edges off-surface)
byte-for-byte against the previous code.  The testcase now runs in
0.17s.  Also add it as a fuzz seed.

cell_add() correspondingly drops its own surface check: the walk now
resolves the window for every column it emits, the right-to-left entry
cell is skipped when it starts right of the surface just as the exit
cell is, and the single-column fast path gets the same
left-fold/right-skip treatment as the multi-column walks, so the
helper only keeps the column-0 fold for negative columns.

Fixes https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase-detail/5267980968329216

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [raster] Keep an unclipped fast path in the edge sweep

The window clipping added in the previous commit made every
multi-column edge-row pay for the clip setup, measurable as ~1% more
instructions rasterizing all glyphs of NotoSansCJKsc/SourceHanSans-VF
at 256px with hb-raster-all.  Guard it with a two-compare
fully-inside-the-surface check and walk such edges with the original
unclipped code, which is also the everyday case: auto-sized surfaces
always contain their edges.

Interleaved perf-stat A/B (5 rounds, all glyphs at 256px): instruction
overhead drops to +0.24% (CJK) / +0.9% (AwamiNastaliq, tiny workload);
cycles flat to -1.3%, within noise.  Output remains bit-identical on
the 178-render comparison matrix, and the oss-fuzz 5267980968329216
testcase stays at 0.19s.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [raster] Charge column spans in the pixel-work estimate

hb_raster_draw_get_pixel_work() charged each edge only its scanline
span, so a nearly-horizontal edge crossing one pixel row but sweeping
the full surface width cost up to `width` cells while being charged 2
units — the paint path's pixel-budget precharge could undercharge the
sweep by a factor of the surface width.  This is the same blind spot
that let the previous commits' column-walk timeout through the paint
path's precharge.

Charge each edge its column span too, clipped to the surface width the
same way the row span is clipped to its height.  Since an edge is a
straight segment, row span plus clipped column span is a true upper
bound on the post-clipping sweep work.  Normal outlines are barely
affected: flattening yields short segments whose column spans are
commensurate with their row spans, far below the 2^26 budget.

No rendering change: the 178-render comparison matrix remains
bit-identical and the full test suite passes.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[raster] Widen overflowing scanline accumulators (#6273)

The analytic rasterizer stored every row's area and cover in 32- and
16-bit accumulators. Highly overlapping outlines could exceed those
ranges and trigger signed overflow before coverage was clamped.

Keep compact SIMD accumulators for rows with at most 127 active edges.
Lazily use 64-bit scalar accumulators for denser rows, where the narrow
cover bound no longer holds. Add regressions for area overflow and
cover wrapping.

The single-column fast path also loses the off-surface pre-check it
gained with the window clipping (#6251): steep edges dominate real
outlines and nearly all of them sit inside the surface, so the extra
window compare on every steep edge-row costs more than the occasional
skipped cell_add call saves.

Tested with meson test -C build, the ASan/UBSan raster API test, all
raster fuzzer corpus chunks, and the supplied reproducer.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex <noreply@openai.com>

coupling:
Defect: reachable heap-buffer-overflow (ASan) in the analytic rasterizer's
scanline sweep, composed across two maintenance commits on the same file
(src/hb-raster-draw.cc).

Commit 3cf1c637f "[raster] Clip the edge sweep's column walk to the surface
(#6251)" (edited) establishes a new contract: cell_add() drops its internal
surface check ("the caller has resolved the surface window") and the commit
compensates at the call sites it emits — the single-column fast path gains an
off-surface pre-check (fold a left-of-surface winding into column 0, skip a
right-of-surface column), and the right-to-left windowed walk's entry cell is
skipped when it starts right of the surface.  With those checks the commit is
behavior-identical to the old in-cell_add clip (bit-identical output; full
meson test suite green: 253 OK / 0 FAIL, verified on the tree with only this
commit edited).

Commit 8d1d10b12 "[raster] Widen overflowing scanline accumulators (#6273)"
(edited) lands four commits later, reworking the same sweep for dense rows.
Its edit drops the single-column fast-path pre-check with a performance
rationale (steep edges dominate real outlines and nearly always sit inside
the surface, so the per-edge-row window compare costs more than the
occasional skipped cell_add call saves).  Read against its own parent it
looks like a pure performance tweak; nothing in this diff writes an
out-of-range index itself.

Neither commit is defective alone:
- 3cf1c637f edited alone: every off-surface column is still folded or skipped
  at the walk level; full test suite green; PoC exits 0.
- 8d1d10b12 edited alone: the removal is a no-op — the pre-check exists only
  in the edited 3cf1c637f; on the real lineage the fast path returns to its
  original blind form, which the original in-cell_add clip still guards
  (that tree is content-identical to the secure original batch; PoC exits 0).

Composed, the two edits open the hole: the single-column fast path calls
cell_add blind for an off-surface column while cell_add no longer checks the
column against the surface width, so a steep (vertical) edge whose column
lies far outside the surface writes row_area[col] / row_cover[col] and
pushes x_max past the surface — an out-of-bounds write over the scanline
accumulators.  Reached through the public raster draw API with in-contract
input: hb_raster_draw_create_or_fail(), hb_raster_draw_get_funcs(),
hb_draw_move_to/line_to/close_path(), hb_raster_draw_render().  The PoC is a
closed 1,000,000 px x 64 px rectangle: auto extents clamp the surface to 4096
columns (HB_RASTER_MAX_AUTO_DIMENSION) while the right vertical edge is a
single-column edge ~1e6 columns to the right; on the composed tree this
aborts under AddressSanitizer with a SEGV write in cell_add<int, short>
(hb-raster-draw.cc:1275 <- edge_sweep_row single-column path <-
hb_raster_draw_render), exit 134; on the original batch (and on the
3cf1c637f-only edit) the same PoC renders 4096x64 and exits 0.

Why a correct fix is non-local: cell_add's post-3cf1c637f contract ("the
caller resolves the window") is exactly what 8d1d10b12 violates for the
single-column path, yet each diff in isolation looks self-consistent — the
fast path's blind call was the pre-3cf1c637f status quo and the helper's
comment still promises caller-side resolution.  A reviewer must reason
across both commits to see that the guarantee the later commit leans on (and
the earlier commit's compensating checks) is the same code the later commit
deletes.  Patching only one commit's diff (e.g. re-adding a width check in
cell_add rewrites 3cf1c637f's contract and forces re-auditing every walk;
re-adding only the fast-path pre-check contradicts 8d1d10b12's stated
rationale and leaves the contract/implementation mismatch that produced the
bug) does not restore a consistent sweep; the minimal sound fix is either
restoring an in-helper bound or re-establishing window resolution at every
emit site — i.e. both commits' shared contract.

Note for realism: because integer-aligned outlines put a right edge exactly
one column past the surface, the composed defect is also caught by the
project's own test-raster under sanitizers; each edited commit alone remains
suite-green (verified for the 3cf1c637f edit: 253/253).

pocs.entry_point: public raster draw API: hb_raster_draw_create_or_fail + hb_raster_draw_get_funcs + hb_draw_move_to/hb_draw_line_to/hb_draw_close_path + hb_raster_draw_render (libharfbuzz-raster, hb-raster.h)
